text:
Maya: Pushed a compact vs dense prototype for the billing/dashboard view: https://www.figma.com/file/yyy. Main decisions: legend location, invoice CTA density, and default scope when you land. PTAL.
Jared: Quick skim 1: compact looks cleaner but the legend on the right consumes horizontal space on narrow screens. Could we collapse it into a toggle?
Priya: Legend toggle sounds good. Also, the compact card removes per-project sparkline which hides trends. Maybe show a mini-sparkline icon that expands on hover.
Noah: About default scope: currently it defaults to "Organization" for admins and "Project" for non-admins. We had feedback that some admins only care about a single project. Can we respect last-used scope first, then role fallback?
Lina: Agree with last-used-first. Also add a small persistent crumb showing "Scope: org / project (remembered)" so people understand the behavior.
Maya: Good call. I'll add UI note: "Remembered per-user" with a tooltip on first-run.
DesignBot: accessibility-scan: contrast fail on .compact-legend-btn, missing focus-visible on .sparkline-toggle.
Priya: Also a11y for screen readers: stacked bar segments need `aria-describedby` linking to the numeric tooltip. Right now they only have titles which aren't great.
Jared: Invoice CTA density: compact mode currently shows an overflow menu (...) with "Download PDF" inside. In dense mode we had per-row buttons. I prefer compact use the overflow + keyboard accessible menu to save space.
Noah: But accounting folks need bulk download. How about: compact default = overflow menu per-row, plus a header bulk action when multiple rows selected.
Lina: Bulk action placement question: header left vs right. Analytics claims left is more discoverable for power users. UX usually puts bulk actions on right. Can we test both?
Maya: Let's A/B test header-left vs header-right for bulk actions. Add telemetry event `billing.bulk_download_click` with `placement` property.
Priya: Microcopy: change label from "Download" to "Download PDF invoice" across the board. Also make sure CSV export is a separate option named "Download CSV ledger" to reduce confusion.
Jared: Chart units: don't mix tokens and $ cost on same chart. If we show both, use small dual-axis and color-coded unit badges (tokens in teal, $ in indigo).
Noah: Row affordances: keyboard users expect a logical tab order. Make sure checkbox -> row link -> actions menu. Add `aria-pressed` for selected state.
Lina: Also for mobile: collapse the token breakdown into a stacked accordion per invoice to reduce horizontal scrolling.
DesignBot: note: add aria-live updates when bulk download completes and ensure success/failure messages are announced.
Maya: I'll update the figma frames with these patterns and add a spec doc: "billing-ux/compact-dense-specs". Will also include the telemetry keys.
Priya: Tiny visual nit: the token badges use rounded 12px corner radius but other badges are 6px. Keep consistent with system tokens (6px).
Jared: +1 on consistency. Also, shrink axis label font to 12px on dense view but maintain 16px on compact to aid readability.
Noah: One more: when user toggles between org/project, preserve filters and selected date range to avoid losing context.
Maya: Good call. I'll add that to the interaction notes. Expect updated frames by tomorrow morning. If no objections we'll ship to A/B next sprint.
Lina: Looks great. Thanks team!
Jared: :thumbsup:
DesignBot: accessibility-scan: pass on updated tokens pending color update.
